Subject: GleamTech hosted pricing — consumption snapshot & next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and asks so we’re aligned on numbers before I pull pricing scenarios together: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use case: search + summarization microservice for internal knowledge and customer support.
- Average response size: ~80–100 tokens (snippet + short summary).
- Traffic shape: low steady background, spikes during office hours and product launches.

Numbers you shared (please confirm):
- Average sustained QPS: ~0.5 req/s
- Peak QPS observed in testing: ~6 req/s (short windows, ~5–10 mins)
- Target production start: early Sept, pilot in Aug

Quick math I ran (please verify):
- Avg tokens per request: 90 tokens
- Avg token/sec = 0.5 * 90 = 45 tokens/sec => ~3.9M tokens/day => ~118M tokens/month
- Peak token/sec (peak QPS 6 * 90) = 540 tokens/sec (short bursts)

What I need from you to finalize pricing options:
1) Confirm the average tokens/request (90 is my assumption from the call)
2) Attach any CSV with daily/hourly test traffic (you mentioned you’d share a CSV)
3) Target $/1M tokens you’re comfortable with or budget range for the pilot month

I’ve attached a lightweight pricing template (redwood_pricing_scenarios.xlsx) with a few commitment bands (monthly commit, burst allowance, and pay-as-you-go) — I’ll populate once I get the confirmed numbers.

Next steps proposed:
- Aisha: send consumption CSV and confirm avg tokens/request and peak windows (today)
- Ben: return 2–3 pricing scenarios and a recommended SLA/burst plan (by Mon EOD)

Thanks — I’ll keep Marissa and Karthik in the loop for thresholds and billing ops.

—
Ben Carter

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers and attaching the CSV you asked for (gleamtech_consumption_breakdown.csv). A few notes inline: 

- Average tokens/request: 88 tokens (we re-ran a sample against the prod model; median 82, mean 88).
- Average sustained QPS (current test harness): ~0.45 req/s (we expect this to grow during pilot).
- Peak observed in our stress test: 5.8 req/s sustained for ~7 minutes, and occasional short bursts up to ~9 req/s for ~1–2 minutes during query storms.
- Pilot target: 1st week of September; 2-week pilot with ~100 users.
- Budget band for pilot: flexible but aim to keep us < $4k for pilot month. (Open to a committed pilot discount.)

I’m attaching the CSV with hourly bins from our last 14-day test. Let me know if you want raw logs.

A couple of asks for Redwood:
1) Can you show a 3-month ramp committed option and a 1-month trial with overage pricing?
2) Any recommended burst protection settings to avoid throttling during launches?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,

Subject: Re: GleamTech hosted pricing — consumption snapshot & next steps

Aisha — got the CSV, thanks. I did a quick pass with Marissa and Karthik and sketched 3 scenarios (attached in redwood_pricing_scenarios.xlsx):

Scenario A — Trial (1 month)- Monthly commit: 50M tokens- Unit price: $22 / 1M tokens for committed portion- Overage: $30 / 1M tokens- Burst allowance: up to 2x sustained for 10 minutes / day- Estimated spend (based on your CSV): ~$1,900

Scenario B — Starter Commit (3 months ramp)- Monthly commit: 120M tokens- Unit price: $15 / 1M tokens- Overage: $20 / 1M tokens- Burst allowance: up to 3x sustained for 30 minutes / day- Estimated spend (based on current profile): ~$1,800 / month (month 1), scales with usage

Scenario C — Production (12 month)- Monthly commit: 600M tokens- Unit price: $9 / 1M tokens- Overage: $12 / 1M tokens- SLA: 99.9% with reserved concurrency lane and priority routing- Estimated spend: depends on ramp; good for 6–12 months forecasted growth

Key notes on tokens / TPS (from your CSV):
- Estimated monthly tokens (current baseline): ~97M tokens / month
- Average sustained QPS: ~0.45–0.5 req/s
- Peak short-burst token TPS: up to ~810 tokens/sec (9 req/s * 90 tokens)

Recommendation: For your stated pilot and budget ask, Scenario A gets you into a controlled pilot under $2k. Scenario B is the best value if you’re confident in a multi-month ramp — it hits a ~ $15 / 1M unit and gives more burst headroom. We can do a limited 30-day trial credit toward a Starter Commit if procurement is OK.

Next steps:
- Aisha: confirm which scenario you prefer and whether procurement needs a PO or SOW (reply to thread)
- Ben/Marissa: if Starter or Production, we’ll prepare a draft commitment (DocuSign link) and reserved-lane config for your infra team

I’ll also propose burst/protection defaults for your account: 3x sustained with token-leakback for short spikes, and automated fallback to a light model if sustained over threshold for >5 minutes. Karthik — can you add those defaults to the spreadsheet and highlight what would be configurable in Private vs Hosted?

—
Ben

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. Devon and I reviewed the scenarios and we’re leaning to Scenario B (Starter Commit) because the unit econ hits our target and it gives predictable budget for the pilot-to-prod ramp. A few procurement asks before we sign: 

- Can we get a 30-day trial credit applied to month 1 (we’d like to keep pilot spend < $4k)?
- Please add a short clause for overage notification (email + webhook) when usage >90% of commit for 72h.
- We need an exported CSV template for billing line items for our finance team (monthly token breakdown by model and by route).

If you can add those items to the DocuSign draft I think we can move forward next week. Also looping Marissa to confirm reserved-lane config and any limits on burst credits.

Happy to have Devon jump on a short call with Karthik to dial the burst settings.

Best —
Aisha
